extraction.name: Stanford Question Answering Dataset (SQuAD)
extraction.description: A reading comprehension dataset consisting of 100,000+ questions posed by crowdworkers on a set of Wikipedia articles, where the answer to each question is a segment of text from the corresponding reading passage.
extraction.creator: Pranav Rajpurkar, Jian Zhang, Konstantin Lopyrev, Percy Liang
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was collected in three stages: curating passages from Wikipedia, crowdsourcing question-answers on those passages, and obtaining additional answers.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: If a question was not answerable by a span in the paragraph, workers were asked to submit the question without marking an answer. Over the development and test sets, 2.6% of questions were marked unanswerable by at least one of the additional crowdworkers.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Top 10,000 articles of English Wikipedia based on internal PageRanks.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: From each of the sampled Wikipedia articles, individual paragraphs were extracted by stripping away images, figures, tables, and discarding paragraphs shorter than 500 characters.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Individual paragraphs were extracted from the articles, stripping away images, figures, tables, and discarding paragraphs shorter than 500 characters.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Crowdworkers were tasked with asking and answering up to 5 questions on the content of a paragraph. Questions were entered in a text field, and answers were highlighted in the paragraph. Workers were encouraged to ask questions in their own words.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Daemo platform (with Amazon Mechanical Turk backend)
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: At least 2 additional answers were obtained for each question in the development and test sets to evaluate human performance and robustness. 2.6% of questions were marked unanswerable by at least one additional crowdworker.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: At least 3 for development and test sets (1 original + at least 2 additional).
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Located in the United States or Canada, with a 97% HIT acceptance rate and a minimum of 1000 HITs.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Questions with span-based answers are more constrained than the more interpretative questions found in more advanced standardized tests.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, development, and testing of reading comprehension models.

name.evidence: We present the Stanford Question Answering Dataset (SQuAD), a new reading comprehension dataset...

description.evidence: We present the Stanford Question Answering Dataset (SQuAD), a new reading comprehension dataset consisting of 100,000+ questions posed by crowdworkers on a set of Wikipedia articles, where the answer to each question is a segment of text from the corresponding reading passage.

url.evidence: The dataset is freely available athttps://stanford-qa.com .

creator.evidence: Pranav Rajpurkar and Jian Zhang and Konstantin Lopyrev and Percy Liang

inLanguage.evidence: obtain the top 10000 articles of English Wikipedia

rai:dataCollection.evidence: We collect our dataset in three stages: curating passages, crowdsourcing question-answers on those passages, and obtaining additional answers.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: To retrieve high-quality articles, we used Project Nayuki’s Wikipedia’s intemal PageRanks to obtain the top 10000 articles of English Wikipedia... Next, we employed crowdworkers to create questions.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: To retrieve high-quality articles, we used Project Nayuki’s Wikipedia’s intemal PageRanks to obtain the top 10000 articles of English Wikipedia, from which we sampled 536 articles uniformly at random.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: From each of these articles, we extracted individual paragraphs, stripping away images, figures, tables, and discarding paragraphs shorter than 500 characters.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: On each paragraph, crowdworkers were tasked with asking and answering up to 5 questions on the content of that paragraph. The questions had to be entered in a text field, and the answers had to be highlighted in the paragraph... Additionally, crowdworkers were encouraged to ask questions in their own words, without copying word phrases from the paragraph.

rai:dataAnnotationPlatform.evidence: We used the Daemo platform (Gaikwad et al., 2015), with Amazon Mechanical Turk as its backend.

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: To get an indication of human performance on SQuAD and to make our evaluation more robust, we obtained at least 2 additional answers for each question in the development and test sets... Over the development and test sets, 2.6% of questions were marked unanswerable by at least one of the additional crowdworkers.

rai:annotationsPerItem.evidence: we obtained at least 2 additional answers for each question in the development and test sets.

rai:annotatorDemographics.evidence: Crowdworkers were required to have a 97% HIT acceptance rate, a minimum of 1000 HITs, and be located in the United States or Canada.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: While questions with span-based answers are more constrained than the more interpretative questions found in more advanced standardized tests, we still find a rich diversity of questions and answer types in SQuAD.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: We partitioned the articles randomly into a training set (80%), a development set (10%), and a test set (10%).
